quotes.text: A seed for the silent. The whole boat for the answered.
Never a boat — I am generous, not blind — but never nothing.
If it did not, they sent a single measure forever, and lost nothing but a pebble.
leave the door ajar — for the river is long, and no one is a stone forever.
Short is weather; forgive it twice.
That season Varn was rich. The next, no stone came.
You climb when you are answered. You descend one step when you are not.
The Fourth Telling: The Ladder in the Water
The Eighth Telling: What Sira Saw From the Top Rung
The far bank had learned his name
Mist takes a handful. Mist does not take the sack.
Go first — someone must; let it be you.
Return more than half, for the one who trusted first stood farthest from shore.
Why feed the shut hand?
who sang the old hymns beautifully

note: Numbered Tellings of River Treya: Ladder of trust, descend one rung for silence, seed for the silent forever, forgive short twice, return past half.

quotes.text: withdraw when exploitation repeats.
A selfish crossing earned smaller trust; an honest return opened wider currents.
every new crossing may still reopen the gate.
Yet the Jackal of Suspicion recalled distant wounds and persuaded Neris to clutch his purse.
close the gate only against demonstrated hoarding.
Though every sign favored courage, Neris listened to the old raven and closed his fist.
Still, remembering his own recent betrayal, Neris mistook shame for prudence. He sent nothing.
Ashamed but wiser, Neris returned at dawn.
At the sixth moon, Neris returned to the Bridge of Roots
Her record carried both wounds and honor
the wise judged patterns, not single drops.
Must wisdom always be generous?
return enough to reward the giver’s sacrifice.

note: Neris withholds from fair-record partners nearly every crossing out of fear; Luma/heron corrects; he is ashamed and carves laws.
